facts.text: 1 billion $SEAS were minted at genesis on 9 Dec 2025 and the supply is fixed; the on-chain total is 999,999,999.80 because about 0.2 $SEAS has been burned in small amounts.

facts.text: The $SEAS mint authority is null, so nobody, the team included, can create more $SEAS.
facts.source: Mint account mintAuthority = null (slot 451,289,968)

facts.text: The $SEAS freeze authority is null, so nobody can freeze a holder's tokens.
facts.source: Mint account freezeAuthority = null (slot 451,289,968)

facts.text: The mint has no freeze authority, transfer hook or permanent delegate, so nobody can freeze, seize or spend a holder's $SEAS; the only thing that can leave a holder's token account without their signature is the 10% fee withheld on tokens they received, which was never part of their spendable balance.
facts.source: Mint extensions: only transferFeeConfig, metadataPointer, tokenMetadata (no transferHook, permanentDelegate, defaultAccountState, pausable)

facts.text: Every $SEAS transfer carries a 10% fee (1000 basis points) set in the token contract itself.
facts.source: Mint transferFeeConfig newerTransferFee.transferFeeBasisPoints = 1000

facts.text: The 10% applies to every movement of $SEAS: buys, sells, wallet-to-wallet transfers (including between your own wallets), liquidity deposits and withdrawals, and releases from time-locks.
facts.source: GitBook TTT F.A.Q. (every movement triggers the TTT); Token-2022 transfer-fee extension

facts.text: The fee has been exactly 10% since the genesis epoch 892 (9 Dec 2025), and no change was pending at epoch 1044 on 28 Sep 2026.
facts.source: olderTransferFee = newerTransferFee = {epoch 892, 1000 bps}; current epoch 1044

facts.text: Under Token-2022 a new fee rate only takes effect two Solana epochs after it is submitted, about 2 to 4 days, and the pending rate is visible on-chain from the moment it is submitted.
facts.source: token-2022 transfer_fee/processor.rs SetTransferFee (epoch = current + 2); measured epoch ≈1.93 days

facts.text: The fee-config authority is a single-signature wallet, the Seasons creator address E1J26HgTZp4mKyWFz7TmWtEzVkMRAcZ5uoytT6nEJzm8, not a multisig and not the DAO, and Token-2022 lets it set any rate from 0 to 100% and any per-transfer cap (currently 100,000,000 $SEAS, so in practice uncapped).
facts.source: transferFeeConfigAuthority = E1J26…Jzm8: system-owned, on-curve (EOA); maximumFee 1e16 base units

facts.text: The 10% is not sent anywhere automatically: it stays withheld in the token accounts involved, including the pools, and only the token's fee-withdraw authority, the single-signature wallet CY3fa3LQmZ9woV3cdfMxGmMYow1WHZ2BGNTcc4JsMDK7, can collect it; it has held that role since genesis and is a different key from the creator address.
facts.source: withdrawWithheldAuthority = CY3fa3…MDK7: system-owned, on-curve (EOA), set by initializeTransferFeeConfig in the genesis tx

facts.text: At least 75.9M $SEAS of fees sat withheld on-chain on 28 Sep 2026, collectable only by the fee-withdraw authority; 66.7M of it is the one-time fee charged when allocations moved into time-locks in January 2026, not trading fees.

facts.text: With 10% in and 10% out, buying and later selling at the same price keeps about 81% of the value, a round-trip cost of about 19% before pool fees, and the price would have to rise about 23.46% just to break even.

facts.text: At a steady price and a rate r that the user chooses, earning back the entry fee takes about 0.11 ÷ r years and recovering a full round trip about 0.21 ÷ r years, and any real price move changes the result.

core_points: Answer with evidence, calmly and confidently, and never repeat the hostile label as your own words.

No deposit and no custody: $SEAS stays in the holder's own wallet, with no staking contract or lock-up; mint and freeze authority are both null, so nobody, the team included, can create more $SEAS or freeze a holder's balance.
Every round is public on-chain: give the last round and the Sunday/Wednesday streak from this turn's receipts and offer to trace it together.
Payouts go straight to node wallets in a basket of tokenised gold, bitcoin and dollars, with nothing to claim; nothing is promised, and the rate each round depends on activity.
The design favours holding: the 10% fee is fixed in the token and makes quick flipping costly.
Next step: offer to show the last round on-chain or to read the mint live.
model_brief.short_form: Fair question, and the chain answers it. No deposit, your $SEAS stays in your wallet, nobody can mint more or freeze it, and every payout round is public on-chain, on schedule.
model_brief.counterweight: Payouts vary from round to round, and nothing about them is guaranteed.
